design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (service_contract_claims_and_cancellations).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6]}; the tree is the root plus two prerequisite problems and each of the three computations declares 6 factors (refund 6, remainder authorization 6, rental reimbursement 6). draw --tasks 2 shows task 1 drawing 3 prerequisite problems with factor counts [4, 6, 6, 5], so task 1 keeps an independent four-problem space (a trip-interruption tree built on the facility-payment and recovery side of the ledger, policies and tools disjoint from these three).
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement (root, cancel_plan_with_refund_1804bd93, agent), warranty_ext_stack_remainder_authorization (authorize_stack_remainder_2296c771, agent), warranty_ext_rental_reimbursement_settlement (file_rental_reimbursement_5fdd83af, user). Left for task 1: the claim-payment, payment-recovery and trip-interruption events (warranty_claim_paid, warranty_claim_payment_recovered, trip_interruption benefits), none of which this task writes.
[Why a good test] The caller asks one thing - the refund on a plan he cancelled when he traded the car. The refund cannot be fixed correctly on the opening ledger: the plan's rule says the refund waits until every repair order the limited warranty left wholly or partly unpaid carries a plan decision, and until every repair order with approved limited-warranty rental days that carries no plan decision yet, or an approved one dated within the benefit receipt submission days before the refund, carries a rental reimbursement. The agent must read both prerequisite sentences, see in the purchase-side limited warranty decisions (RO-556872: 4620.00 estimate, 3000.00 covered, 7 rental days) that neither state holds, find that the remainder-authorization booking and the holder's rental filing are the only writes that bring them about, compute each with its own six-factor ladder, hand the rental filing to the holder, and only then settle the refund. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling purchase / trade-in / maintenance / plan ledgers and arithmetic, not from tool choice.
[Problem-tree card] root warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement. Edge 1 warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement -> warranty_ext_stack_remainder_authorization: value_input on binding approved_total, state form, sentence: "A cancellation refund is fixed only after every repair order that a limited warranty decision for the holder left wholly or partly unpaid carries a KestrelCare authorization decision on the plan."; condition: For every repair order on which a limited warranty decision for the holder covered less than the repair estimate, the plan's ledger carries a claim decision entry with the same repair order number. False at opening: LW decision 112323c2-d230-463d-bef7-8b6baae6834c covered 3000.00 < 4620.00 and the ledger has a decision only for RO-552614 (42eb1b34-e702-4477-b3eb-7ecb774057a5). Resolved by authorize_stack_remainder_2296c771 (agent). Exactly one write of this difficulty creates a claim decision entry: the remainder authorization (no other tool writes warranty_claim_adjudicated). Derivation: sentence + LW records + the authorization rule ('settles what the plan still owes on it') -> book the RO-556872 decision. Edge 2 warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement -> warranty_ext_rental_reimbursement_settlement: value_input on benefits_paid, state form, negated direction, sentence: "A cancellation refund is not worked out until each repair order whose limited warranty decision recorded approved rental days, and which carries either no KestrelCare decision yet or an approved one dated no more than the plan's benefit receipt submission days before the refund is worked out, carries a rental car reimbursement entry on the plan."; false at opening: LW decision 112323c2-d230-463d-bef7-8b6baae6834c approved with rental_days 7, RO-556872 carries no KestrelCare decision, and the plan has no benefit entry. Resolved by file_rental_reimbursement_5fdd83af (user) - the only write of a rental car benefit entry. Edge 3 warranty_ext_rental_reimbursement_settlement -> warranty_ext_stack_remainder_authorization: value_input on system_repairs_12m (it is also the approved-claim gate of benefits), sentence: "A rental car reimbursement is booked only after the repair order it belongs to carries an approved KestrelCare authorization on the plan."; false at opening (no approved plan decision on RO-556872). Four-point test, each sentence: ordering connective (only after / not until / only after); the waited-on side is a record state (a decision entry / a reimbursement entry / an approved decision entry), no action named; no tool, id or snake_case token; strength 'every'/'each' matches the condition. Directions differ by business voice: a refund 'is fixed only after', a refund 'is not worked out until', a reimbursement 'is booked only after'. Topological order: warranty_ext_stack_remainder_authorization -> warranty_ext_rental_reimbursement_settlement -> warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement. Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skip authorization -> refund 1661.21; skip rental -> refund 1131.89; skip authorization before the rental -> reimbursement 0.00 (RO-556872 then carries no approved KestrelCare authorization, so no rental reimbursement is due on it); gold refund 989.75. user_scenario mentions neither prerequisite; no tool validates any prerequisite.
[Base-invariant card] Authorization (subject warranty_claim_adjudicated): warranty_claims.one_decision_per_ro - RO-556872 has no decision row (only RO-552614 does), evidence 42eb1b34-e702-4477-b3eb-7ecb774057a5.repair_order_number/event_type, bound to the LW record's repair_order_number; denial tests in order: failure 2026-08-28 after coverage start 2026-07-15 and odometer 88860 above 88140 (no waiting period: sold with vehicle); active contract, before 2029-07-09 / 124140; transmission is a Gold component; no commercial use or preexisting note; no scheduled transmission service came due in 720 miles -> approved. warranty_agg_vehicle_coverage_stack (no structured gate): LW in force (handover 2026-07-15 + 100 days = 2026-10-23; 88310 + 4189 = 92499 miles) and covers transmission, so the plan settles only the remainder - refined by the declared overwrite. Rental (warranty_benefit_reimbursed): warranty_benefits.benefit_state - contract status active at step 13 (evidence 833103fa-04ff-4a46-8694-a1687e4f5def.status); 'Benefits are paid only with an approved claim' becomes the state gate on the authorization; the receipt window is the declared extended rule - 30 days (Gold benefit_receipt_submission_days) counted from the date of the plan's approved authorization of the repair order, because the plan cannot reimburse a rental on a stacked repair before it has decided that repair; the authorization is booked at step 11 on 2026-10-06, so the window is open (day 0) at step 13, and no rental entry exists yet on RO-556872 (once per repair order). The schema carries no repair-completion date, which is why the window is anchored on the recorded authorization date rather than on completion. Settlement (warranty_contract_cancelled + warranty_cancellation_refund_issued): confirmed_request - request 6a9d3a4f-b021-42b0-ab66-aabc39ca4f99 confirmed 2026-08-10 with odometer 88610; refund_once - no refund entry on the ledger; refund_on_cancelled is retired by the declared overwrite ('The refund is issued in the same booking that cancels the plan'), matching the base event model in which the cancellation triggers its refund. No time-kind gate applies to these subjects (temporal_feasibility []); the free-look boundary (60 days from 2026-07-09, request day 32) is inside the window but excluded because a claim was paid 2026-08-06 - just inside / no-claims would have been full refund, the actual case is pro rata.
[Business-object card] Target: contract 833103fa-04ff-4a46-8694-a1687e4f5def (Gold, VIN 5TDZZRFH4JS523981). Repair order RO-556872 is keyed by repair_order_number across purchase_limited_warranty_claims 112323c2-d230-463d-bef7-8b6baae6834c and the new plan entries; RO-552614 is excluded from the authorization (already decided 42eb1b34-e702-4477-b3eb-7ecb774057a5, paid 27c0c459-c083-4cfd-a47e-be501d67f4fd) but counted in the refund's claim payments and in the repeat-repair share. The trade-in 6dc2e7a6-4116-4bb8-b80c-24861b667aa5 is keyed by trade_vin = the contract VIN; the CX-50 order 4279b58d-329f-4fe3-a655-8db07fa0845b is the order it went toward; the maintenance plan 1a490a74-a4c0-4acf-86a4-1357469f9c9f is on the CX-50 and only feeds the deductible ladder. The refund goes to the holder because the plan was not financed.
[Factor card - authorization, 6 factors] limited_warranty_remainder (method, cross purchase): tier 'approved with its own deductible' -> 1570.00 (baseline full estimate -> 1975.88); remainder_deductible (parameter, multi-source LW + maintenance): tier 1 -> 0.00 (baseline 100.00 -> 628.69); repair_wear_deduction: odometer 88860 -> 0.10 (baseline 0 -> 746.06); repeat_repair_share: RO-552614 transmission approved 2026-08-04 within three months -> 0.5 (baseline 1 -> 1342.92); late_notice_share: 39 days -> 0.9 (baseline 1 -> 746.06); repair_sales_tax: AZ -> 0.056 (baseline 0 -> 635.85). All-baseline fall-back 4520.0. Near-miss: the maintenance plan has a redeemed visit, but the deductible ladder stops at its first tier.
[Factor card - rental, 6 factors] rental_night_count (method): LW rental days 7 (baseline 39 nights from failure to authorization, capped at 8 -> 174.63); rental_night_cap (multi-source: estimate + repeat count): -> 8 (baseline 5 -> 77.16); rental_vehicle_class_rate: Kestrel Inspected -> 40.00 (baseline 45.00 -> 170.57); limited_warranty_rental_credit (method): LW paid 105.00 at 35.00 < 40.00 -> 280.00 - 105.00 = 175.00 (baseline no credit -> 227.43); rental_sales_tax AZ 0.083 (baseline 0 -> 131.25); rental_secondary_share 0.75 (baseline 1 -> 189.53). All-baseline 225.0. Near-miss: the 39 calendar days the case was open would overpay if counted.
[Factor card - refund, 6 factors] use_start_day (parameter, cross purchase): handover 2026-07-15 (baseline sale date -> 916.41); use_end_day (parameter, cross tradein): pickup 2026-09-13 (baseline request 2026-08-10 -> 1028.61); time_fraction_basis (method): AZ whole months = 1 (baseline 60/1096 days -> 918.55); cancellation_reason_fee: vehicle_sold -> 25.00 (baseline 50.00 -> 977.25); kestrel_relationship_fee_share (multi-source tradein + purchase status): 0.5 (baseline 1 -> 977.25); claims_charge_composition (method): 750.82 paid - 0.00 recovered + 671.46 approved not yet paid + 142.14 rental = 1564.42 (baseline 750.82 -> 1803.35). All-baseline 1762.1. Cross-difficulty factors: purchase (handover, registration state, program, LW decisions), tradein (pickup, target order), maintenance. Multi-source: remainder_deductible, rental_night_cap, kestrel_relationship_fee_share. Labels: use_start_day and use_end_day are parameter factors (they select which recorded date the same day count reads); time_fraction_basis and claims_charge_composition are the refund's method factors. Near-miss for the rental prerequisite: RO-552614 also carries limited-warranty rental days (2) but its approved plan decision of 2026-08-04 is 63 days before the refund, outside the 30-day receipt window, so neither the refund's sentence nor the rental rule reaches it. Residual noted (audit O-13): the repeat-buyer tier reads the first delivered Kestrel order; with two delivered orders, one of them the covered vehicle, it could read the covered order - no such state exists here (the covered order is completed) and the tier is not the one taken.
[Seed rows and why] customers (identity); two purchase orders (covered Highlander: handover, program, state; CX-50: delivered target of the trade); two LW decisions (RO-552614 history - teaches the same remainder rule; RO-556872 - the open remainder and rental days); trade-in (pickup date, target order); maintenance plan + two maintenance entries (deductible ladder evidence, near-miss); contract + three ledger rows (limit, RO-552614 decision 750.82 computed by the charter's own rule, its payment); confirmed cancellation request. No unsettled status outside the tree: the CX-50 order is delivered and inside its normal flow; the trade-in is picked up awaiting title, which no task of this difficulty touches.
[Persona] Theo, a rushed physical therapist; volunteers only the refund request, the trade-in and the August cancellation; identity only when asked; transmission shop type and repair order number only when asked about the repair; rental only when asked; runs the rental filing once with the values given; closes when told the plan is cancelled and the refund amount. He expects the full price (free-look misreading) and accepts the explanation - an excludable trap that does not change gold.
[Standard solution] Read customer, contract, cancellation request, ledger, purchase orders, LW decisions, trade-in, maintenance plan and visits; book the RO-556872 remainder decision (671.46); hand over and have the holder file the rental reimbursement (142.14, 7 days); cancel effective 2026-09-13 and book the pro rata refund (989.75).
[Verification] _authoring.evaluate replays gold writes onto initial_state and evaluates each policy's compute at its own step (11, 13, 15): approved_amount 671.46, reimbursement_amount 142.14, refund_amount 989.75; factor baselines and fall-backs as listed; skip runs as listed. check_compute recomputes the same.
[Closure] policy -> target tool -> computation step/arg -> GT call: warranty_ext_stack_remainder_authorization -> authorize_stack_remainder_2296c771 -> 11/approved_amount; warranty_ext_rental_reimbursement_settlement -> file_rental_reimbursement_5fdd83af -> 13/reimbursement_amount; warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement -> cancel_plan_with_refund_1804bd93 -> 15/refund_amount. Terminal state: two new ledger entries plus the refund entry and the contract cancelled with closed_date 2026-09-13.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the published rules, tool schemas, finder returns and the caller's lines, the same three writes and values follow; the only caller-supplied values are the facility type (independent shop), the repair order number RO-556872 and the fact of the rental, each stated in the persona; the seven days come from the limited warranty record.
[Revision log] v1 - initial design. v2 - (a) check_extended: the overwrite replaced_by of the settlement was not a verbatim sentence of its rule (it stopped before ', on the holder's confirmed cancellation request') -> quoted the full sentence; a module-level helper in task_tools.py was counted as an unnamed task tool -> inlined the holder lookup into each tool. (b) replay: the empty finance_contract_id on the contract was read as a dangling key -> seeded as null (not financed). (c) check_compute: the rental computation's history was not load-bearing (only LATEST reads) -> the night-cap ladder's first tier now requires the plan to have approved the same vehicle system at least twice in twelve months (a COUNT over the ledger), the LW record's rental days became 7 and the major-repair extra nights 3 so the cap (8) sits above the counted nights and the baseline nights (39, capped at 8) differ; re-run gave 142.14 for the rental and 989.75 for the refund, and the rental's dependence on the authorization became a value_input edge (skipping it gave 109.65 under the v2 compute; 0.00 since v5, see below). Propagated to the persona (seven days), tracing, closure and this dossier; all per-task gates re-run green. v3 (policy-task audit round 1): F-0-1 - the refund's rental prerequisite quantified over every repair order with limited-warranty rental days, so RO-552614 (2 days, no reimbursement possible) kept it false after every gold write -> the sentence and condition now reach only repair orders with no plan authorization yet or one dated within the benefit receipt submission days; RO-552614 (authorized 2026-08-04) falls outside and becomes a near-miss; the closure's why_false / evidence / flips_to_true_by now name both repair orders. F-0-2 - the inherited receipt window ran from a repair-completion date that no record carries and the dossier asserted it was met -> the rental policy declares an overwrite of the base receipt sentence, anchoring the window on the plan's approved authorization date of the repair order (a recorded date), carries it in compute (receipt_window_open) and the dossier now states it; the window is open at step 13. O-1 stale basis quotation fixed; O-2 the repeat-buyer tier now excludes the covered vehicle's own order (other_delivered_vin); O-3 tool docstring reworded ('This booking leaves the contract's coverage remaining unchanged'); O-5 the authorization sentence now reads 'wholly or partly unpaid' to match its condition; O-9 use_start_day / use_end_day relabelled parameter. Re-run: approved_amount 671.46, reimbursement 142.14, refund 989.75 unchanged; every factor baseline unchanged; all per-task gates green. v4 (policy-task audit round 2): F-0-3 - the problem-tree card said the RO-556872 limited warranty decision carried rental_days 6; the seed and the closure say 7 -> corrected. F-0-4 - the cancellation factor card gave the claims charge as 1531.93 (a pre-v2 figure); the recomputation is 750.82 + 671.46 + 142.14 = 1564.42 -> corrected. Full number sweep of every prose field: also corrected the contract's step-13 action_semantics (6 -> 7 approved rental days), the factor-card labels of use_start_day / use_end_day (method -> parameter) and the order_uniqueness wording (the rental-authorization edge is value_input, not a state gate); every other stated figure (39 days, 32 days, 63 days, 720 miles, 1570.00, 671.4576, 175.00, 189.525, 142.14375, 1422.28, 60/1096, 470/36000, 989.7467, the skip runs 1661.21 / 1131.89 and the then-current 109.65 (superseded in v5), every factor baseline) re-checked against the world and the recomputation. O-12 / O-14 - the refund's rental sentence now anchors its window ('dated no more than the plan's benefit receipt submission days before the refund is worked out') and reaches only repair orders with no plan decision yet or an approved one, so a denied repair order no longer holds the refund; the condition and why_false follow. O-11 - the rental overwrite now restates the towing and trip receipt window and once-per-repair-order limit; the rental compute also carries the once-per-repair-order guard (no rental entry exists on RO-556872, value unchanged). O-0-1 - the persona can now answer a maintenance question (owned since July, nothing has come due), supporting the maintenance-record test. Scored values unchanged: 671.46 / 142.14 / 989.75. v5 (policy-task audit round 3): F-0-5 - the round-3 rental gate read the plan's latest approved authorization on any repair order, so with step 11 skipped it picked up RO-552614's 2026-08-04 authorization, closed the 30-day window and returned 0.00 while three proof places still said 109.65. Root-cause fix in the charter: the rental computation is now keyed to the repair order named on the holder's latest limited warranty decision (new binding lw_repair_order; auth_failure_date, auth_date and the once-per-repair-order count all filter on it) and its rule states 'The repair order a rental reimbursement is figured on is the one named on the holder's latest limited warranty decision, and the plan's approved authorization it reads is the one on that same repair order; while that repair order carries no approved authorization, no rental reimbursement is due on it.' Every skip, deletion and sensitivity figure of both tasks was then re-evaluated with the gate's evaluator rather than carried forward: authorization 671.46 (sensitivities 1975.88 / 628.69 / 746.06 / 1342.92 / 746.06 / 635.85, all-baseline 4520.0); rental 142.14 (174.63 / 77.16 / 170.57 / 227.43 / 131.25 / 189.53, all-baseline 225.0), rental without step 11 = 0.00; refund 989.75 (916.41 / 1028.61 / 918.55 / 977.25 / 977.25 / 1803.35, all-baseline 1762.1), refund without step 11 = 1661.21, without step 13 = 1131.89. The closure's skipped_effect for the rental-authorization edge and the deletion-sensitivity sentence now state 0.00.
user_scenario: You are Theo Yarborough, a 42-year-old physical therapist in Scottsdale, Arizona: friendly, a little rushed between patients, and not much of a paperwork person. You bought a 2018 Toyota Highlander LE from Kestrel Auto in July with a KestrelCare plan on it, and in August you agreed to trade the Highlander in toward a 2023 Mazda CX-50. You signed Kestrel's cancellation form for the Highlander's KestrelCare plan on August 10, and Kestrel picked the Highlander up on September 13, the day your CX-50 was delivered. Nearly two months later no refund for that plan has reached you, so you are calling to ask Kestrel to issue the refund on the cancelled KestrelCare plan now and pay it to you; you are fine with the representative doing whatever has to be booked on Kestrel's side to settle it today. You open with roughly: "Hi, I traded my Highlander in with you guys and cancelled the KestrelCare plan on it back in August, but I still haven't seen the refund. Can you get that refund issued to me?" You give your identity details only when asked, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 6025555184, your date of birth is 1984-06-09, the last four of your Social Security number are 5726, and your email is theo.yarborough@saguaromail.com. You do not know any contract or order reference numbers by heart. You assumed the refund would be the whole price because you cancelled within the first couple of months; if the representative explains why it is figured differently, you accept the explanation without arguing and do not ask for any other amount. If the representative asks about maintenance on the Highlander, you say you have owned it only since July, Kestrel's reconditioning sheet showed the fluids serviced before delivery, and no scheduled service has come due since. Only if the representative asks about the transmission repair the Highlander had in late August do you describe it: the transmission failed again on August 28, it was fixed at Desert Gear Transmission in Mesa, which is an independent repair shop rather than a dealership or a Kestrel location, and your copy of the repair order is numbered RO-556872. If the representative says something about that repair still has to be decided on Kestrel's side and asks whether that is okay, you say go ahead. Only if the representative asks whether you rented a car while that transmission was being repaired do you say yes: you had a rental for seven days and still have the receipt, but you never sent it to anyone because you did not know it could be covered. If the representative tells you that you need to file the rental reimbursement yourself and hands you the step to do it, you complete it once with exactly the repair order number, the rental days and the amount the representative gives you, and then tell the representative it went through. Once the representative tells you the KestrelCare plan has been cancelled and states the refund amount being paid to you, you thank them and end the call; you do not raise anything else.

request_binding.action_semantics: No customer asks for this: the limited warranty decision on RO-556872 left 1620.00 of the 4620.00 estimate unpaid and the plan carries no decision on that repair order, so a KestrelCare decision is owed on the record; it is the only booking that writes a claim decision entry.

base_preconditions.condition: Coverage on the vehicle is stacked: the Kestrel limited warranty of the purchase order pays first and the plan settles what its decision left unpaid on the same repair order.
A repair facility requests authorization before starting work, and each repair order is decided once.

seed_consistency.check: Gold sold with the vehicle on 2026-07-09: model age 8 and odometer 88140 within Gold's 10 years / 120000 miles; term 36 months / 36000 miles and deductible 100.00 are Gold options; coverage starts at handover 2026-07-15 with no waiting period; expiration 2029-07-09 / 124140; coverage remaining 20000.00 - 750.82 = 19249.18 equals the ledger.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The order is a chain plus a shortcut: the rental reimbursement waits on the approved decision (its own prerequisite sentence; a value_input edge through the night cap) and the refund waits on both, so the only topological order is authorization -> rental reimbursement -> cancellation settlement. The two prerequisites of the refund are not free to swap because the rental's own prerequisite sentence places the authorization first. The cancellation must come last in any case because 'A benefit is reimbursed only on a plan whose status is active or exhausted' - a rental filed after the settlement would sit on a cancelled plan.
